question: What are the 7 books included in the Catholic Old Testament that are absent from most Protestant Bibles?

choices.A: Tobit, Judith, 1 & 2 Maccabees, Wisdom, Sirach (Ecclesiasticus), and Baruch
choices.B: Enoch, Jasher, Jubilees, the Didache, the Shepherd of Hermas, the Gospel of Thomas, and Baruch
choices.C: Ezra, Nehemiah, Ruth, Esther, Lamentations, Obadiah, and Jonah
choices.D: Daniel, Ezekiel, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Hosea, Joel, and Amos

teaching.title: The Deuterocanonical Books
teaching.body: Catholics call these seven books 'deuterocanonical' (second canon), while Protestants call them 'Apocrypha' (hidden/spurious). They were in the Septuagint (Greek OT) used by NT authors, included in the Latin Vulgate, and affirmed by African councils (Hippo 393, Carthage 397/419) and the Council of Florence (1441). Luther removed them partly because they support doctrines he opposed (e.g., 2 Maccabees supports purgatory). The Council of Trent (1546) formally defined the Catholic canon including all seven.
